ai.title: Add o3 pro max mode
ai.summary: Introduces `o3` and `o3pro` model support, routing them via `openai.responses` in `ai-sdk.ts` instead of `languageModel`. `thinking-stream.ts` updates stop sequences to include `<write_file>` and injects a distinct prompt for o3 models that enforces early termination when the next action is clear. `common/src/constants.ts` adds short names for `flash-2.5` and `opus-4`.

eli5.text: If you use the latest reasoning model from OpenAI, the assistant now routes your request through a different response system that's better tuned for that model's style. The assistant also stops its internal planning sooner when it can already see the next clear step, so it won't overthink once the path forward is obvious. This mode is live today for anyone able to select that model.

ai.title: Replace manual env setup with Infisical
ai.summary: Migrated environment variable management to Infisical, removing `.env.example` and `@t3-oss/env-core` validation. CI workflows now generate env vars via `scripts/generate-ci-env.js` and `jq` instead of dumping secrets to `.env.local`. Local dev requires Infisical CLI login; `backend/src/env.mjs` deleted in favor of `@/env` alias.

eli5.text: Developers removed the old, manual system for managing passwords and configuration settings, and replaced it with a secure password manager called Infisical. This change affects everyone working on the code, including automated testing systems, and it means that sensitive information like API keys is no longer stored in plain text files. When you look at the project setup, you will need to log in to Infisical using its command-line tool instead of copying a sample settings file. Automated checks and test environments now get their settings through secure scripts that pull from the password manager, removing the risk of leaking secrets.

ai.title: db:migrate uses nx target with optional infisical
ai.summary: common/package.json db:migrate now delegates to nx run common:db-migrate. common/project.json defines db-migrate executor running drizzle-kit push directly if infisical is absent, otherwise via infisical run. Scope limited to common package scripts and Nx project config.

eli5.text: The database setup command now checks whether a special secrets tool is available before running, and falls back to running normally if it isn't. If you're setting up or updating your database, you'll no longer get stuck just because that secrets tool isn't installed - it just skips it and continues. This only affects the database migration step used by developers working in the main shared code folder, and it's in place now.

ai.title: Fix infisical check in drizzle-kit push
ai.summary: Updated `common/project.json` to use POSIX-compliant `>/dev/null 2>&1` redirection instead of Bash-specific `&> /dev/null` for infisical detection. This ensures the drizzle-kit push command executes correctly across different shell environments. The change applies to the `common` package build configuration.

eli5.text: When you run a database update command, the system first checks whether a required password-management tool is installed before deciding how to run it. The instructions for that check were written in a way that only worked in one specific kind of operating system shell, so on certain setups the check could silently fail and the command would run without the expected safety protections. The instructions have been rewritten in a more universally compatible style so the check now works correctly regardless of which shell environment is used. If you looked at the setup file, you would see a single line where the old-style command was replaced with a more standard form near the top of the database-push configuration.

ai.summary: web/package.json routes discord:start and discord:register through nx run web:<target> instead of direct infisical run calls. web/project.json adds nx:run-commands targets for start, discord:start, and discord:register. Each target checks command -v infisical and falls back to bare next start or bun run scripts/discord/*.ts when infisical is absent. Scope limited to web package scripts and project.json targets.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant's Discord bot tools from your computer, they now go through a single project coordinator first, and only try to load your secret environment variables if that coordinator notices the secrets tool is installed. This affects anyone who runs the Discord bot scripts locally. If you looked, you'd see the project's task list now includes a small safety check that runs the bot with the secrets loaded when available, or skips that step and runs the bot directly when the secrets tool isn't installed, instead of always trying to load the secrets and failing.

ai.title: Fix evals import paths and add infisical wrapper
ai.summary: Relative import paths replace absolute module aliases in `evals/git-evals/*` and `evals/scaffolding.ts`. Package scripts in `evals/package.json` now conditionally wrap execution with `infisical run` if the binary exists. `scaffolding.ts` adds a default export for helper functions.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation scripts that test how the assistant performs were having trouble finding the code modules they need to run. They were updated to use relative paths instead of absolute shortcuts, so they can locate shared code across different parts of the project without confusion. Additionally, the test-running commands now automatically use a tool called Infisical to securely access any secrets or credentials needed during testing, if that tool is available. These changes affect the internal team members who run and maintain the evaluation process, ensuring their tests run more reliably and securely.

ai.title: Revert git-evals COSTMODE to normal
ai.summary: Reverts COST_MODE constant from 'experimental' to 'normal' in evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts. This change affects the internal evaluation harness for Git-based tasks. The modification ensures evaluations run under standard cost parameters rather than experimental settings.

eli5.text: The internal system used to test how well Git-based tasks work has switched its cost evaluation setting back from an experimental mode to the standard mode. This means any team running these automated Git-related tests will now get results based on normal, stable parameters instead of the experimental ones previously applied. If someone reviewed the evaluation output today, they would see the testing ran under the default cost settings rather than the experimental configuration that was briefly in place.

ai.title: Fix npm-app deploy env injection and tsconfig
ai.summary: Refactored `npm-app/clean-package.js` to dynamically parse client-side environment keys from `env.ts` instead of hardcoding `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefixes, ensuring correct variable injection into `dist/index.js`. Updated `prepublishOnly` script to run `nx clean` and wrap execution with `infisical run --env=prod`, moving secrets handling out of the root `deploy:npm-app` script. Added `common` to root `tsconfig.json` references and adjusted `common` and `backend` tsconfigs for incremental builds and path resolution.

eli5.text: When developers prepare to publish their assistant app for others to install, the system now automatically discovers which configuration values should be included by reading the settings file directly, instead of guessing based on naming patterns. This means the published version will correctly carry the right environment variables (like which server to connect to) without manual hardcoding. The change also moves the secure secret retrieval step earlier in the process, so passwords and keys are fetched before the app is packaged. This is live today and affects developers who publish the assistant's command-line tool.

eli5.text: The system now quietly logs when its AI helper tool runs into a problem while responding, so developers can see what went wrong in the background. If you're testing this tool on your own computer (not in the live production environment), it will also stop and show you the error immediately instead of trying to keep going. This only affects people building or debugging with the AI helper tools, not regular users chatting with the system.
